about_disease.description: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a neurodegenerative disease characterized by progressive muscular paralysis reflecting degeneration of motor neurons in the primary motor cortex, corticospinal tracts, brainstem and spinal cord.
also_called: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, Parkinsonism/Dementia complex of Guam
Guam Form of Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis
MOTOR NEURON DIS AMYOTROPHIC LATERAL SCLEROSIS
Motor Neuron Disease, Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis

rule_text: Ordered by how strongly the proteins are linked to the disease. Pieces of the same machine count once. If a medicine acts on different machines, the scores are added. Ties: more reports first, then alphabetical. Being first on the list does not mean best.

approved.proof_note: Approved in Japan, according to the database. Moonlight could not find the exact record for this disease.
The database lists this as approved, but gives no regulator record for it.
approved.withdrawal_note: The maker or a regulator has withdrawn this medicine from the market.

proteins.function: Tubulin is the major constituent of microtubules, a cylinder consisting of laterally associated linear protofilaments composed of alpha- and beta-tubulin heterodimers.

being_studied.ending: But there is a catch. Nobody knows from our information if the disease needs this protein turned up or down. So this is a clue to read about. Never start, stop or change any medicine without a doctor.
